issue.title: After upgrading DuckDB to 1.5.2, a delete-heavy transactional stage became significantly slower on the same workload shape
issue.body:
### What happens?

After upgrading DuckDB from 1.4 to 1.5.2, a delete-heavy transactional stage became significantly slower on the same workload shape (I didn't change a single line!)

The pattern is:

Mark a large subset of rows for deletion.
- Delete related rows from a connection table using IN (SELECT ...).
- Delete primary rows.
- Delete dangling rows from a net table.
- Commit one large transaction.

We run specific recipes/pipelines in our system.

Observed runtime regression in our workload (same hardware/config class, same 65GB DB), version baseline(1.4.0) vs new (1.5.2):
- minimal delete set: 277.26s vs 550.44s
- maximum delete set: 549.31s vs 1570.54s # worst impact

### To Reproduce
```python
conn.execute("BEGIN")

conn.execute(
    f"""
    DELETE FROM pex_connection
    WHERE pex_element_id IN (SELECT id FROM pex_element WHERE delete)
    """,
)

conn.execute(
    f"""
    DELETE FROM pex_element
    WHERE delete
    """,
)

conn.execute(
    f"""
    DELETE FROM pex_net
    WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT pex_net_id FROM pex_connection)
    """,
)

conn.execute("COMMIT") # 95% of the time is consumed here
```

### OS:

Linux 5.15.0-177-generic x86_64 (Ubuntu)

### DuckDB Version:

1.4.0 (baseline) vs 1.5.2 (regression observed)

### DuckDB Client:

Python

### Hardware:

Intel Xeon 6724P, 32 CPUs (16 cores / 2 threads), 503 GiB RAM

### Full Name:

Ammar Shahin

### Affiliation:

LENS

### Did you include all relevant configuration (e.g., CPU architecture, Linux distribution) to reproduce the issue?

- [x] Yes, I have

### Did you include all code required to reproduce the issue?

- [x] Yes, I have

### Did you include all relevant data sets for reproducing the issue?

No - I cannot share the data sets because they are confidential

If this is a false positive, feel free to disregard this comment.

Update: I tested version 1.4.4 and noted a similar ~11% improvement in arrow insertion as in 1.5.2, without the decrease in performance during the delete-heavy transactional phase (timing was the same as in 1.4.0).
Hi @ashahinL, thanks for reporting this! A minimal reproducible example would be very helpful to bisect and trace the issue.

Thanks for opening this issue in the DuckDB issue tracker! To resolve this issue, our team needs a reproducible example. This includes:

* A source code snippet which reproduces the issue.
* The snippet should be self-contained, i.e., it should contain all imports and should use relative paths instead of hard coded paths (please avoid `/Users/JohnDoe/...`).
* A lot of issues can be reproduced with plain SQL code executed in the [DuckDB command line client](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/cli/overview). If you can provide such an example, it greatly simplifies the reproduction process and likely results in a faster fix.
* If the script needs additional data, please share the data as a CSV, JSON, or Parquet file. Unfortunately, we cannot fix issues that can only be reproduced with a confidential data set. [Support contracts](https://duckdblabs.com/#support) allow sharing confidential data with the core DuckDB team under NDA.

For more detailed guidelines on how to create reproducible examples, please visit Stack Overflow's ["Minimal, Reproducible Example"](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example) page.

I tried creating a minimal, reproducible Python example, but it gave opposite results.
In the minimal example, version 1.5.2 seems to perform similarly, if not better, than 1.4.0.
Our transactions are much more detailed than what I can illustrate in a simple script, so I'll pause this for now until I can replicate a similar transaction.
